title: P19: cosine pretraining decay to zero learning rate
description: P19: change only the pretraining cosine learning-rate floor from 0.1 to 0.0 of the unchanged 1e-3 peak. A quieter final checkpoint may preserve coherent proof features that enable more successful exploration and adaptation during the fixed downstream RL procedure.
hypothesis: Reducing late-pretraining update noise may improve the starting policy for expert iteration without sacrificing model capacity or increasing weight decay. Baseline validation loss flattens well before the 300-second endpoint; stronger decay (013), reduced-capacity sharing (014), and slower AdamW second moments (015) failed to improve the three-seed mean. No prior registration changes the cosine floor. This intervention lowers the entire post-warmup cosine trajectory, especially its tail, and also reduces integrated AdamW decay because decay is learning-rate scaled; it is not a pure endpoint-noise isolation. Less late plasticity could instead impair exploration. Downstream dev-transfer performance alone determines keep/discard.
expected_delta: Central prediction +5 to +15 dev-transfer theorems at true length >=7 versus baseline 012 (exact mean 147.67; stored rounded mean 148), with plausible downside -25. Keep only if the seeds 0,1,2 mean improves. No additional operations or parameters: expect negligible direct latency change and approximately 3000 steps in the fixed 300-second pretraining budget; changed generation lengths may still alter RL/evaluation time under the 1200-second cap.
